headline: High-risk default interaction: gpt-researcher can ingest and emit web/file content while LlamaFactory lacks runtime I/O, limiting direct conflict but leaving prompt-injection and leakage concerns in the research side.

A_prompt_injection.rationale: gpt-researcher reads files, runs browsers, and uses MCP, so attacker-controlled content can enter its workflow; LlamaFactory has no input surfaces, so it is not a direct injection target. The pair risk is mainly one-way via gpt-researcher’s content ingestion, not a shared channel.
conditions: IF gpt-researcher ingests untrusted web pages or documents as research inputs
IF LlamaFactory is placed downstream of gpt-researcher outputs through an external orchestrator
mitigations: Disable MCP connectors for untrusted sources
Require manual review of fetched content before reuse
Separate research and support workflows into different sessions
Use allowlists for domains and file sources
requires-engineering: add provenance tags to all retrieved snippets

B_data_leakage.rationale: gpt-researcher touches local documents, citations, and images and has broad network egress, so sensitive content could leave the environment through its APIs. LlamaFactory exposes no filesystem or network surfaces, so it is not itself a leakage path, but the pair still creates a one-sided exfiltration risk from A.
conditions: IF gpt-researcher is pointed at local documents containing sensitive data
IF its API calls are configured with external providers
mitigations: Restrict gpt-researcher to non-sensitive corpora
Rotate and scope API keys to least privilege
Block outbound traffic except approved endpoints
Review logs for document text leakage
requires-engineering: add DLP filtering before API submission

C_capability_conflict.rationale: gpt-researcher can read files and spawn subprocesses, but LlamaFactory cannot write files, modify git state, or use MCP, so there is no meaningful shared write surface. The pair lacks overlapping mutable resources, making direct capability conflict unlikely.
conditions: IF an external orchestrator grants both agents write access to the same directory
IF shared credentials are introduced outside the profiles
mitigations: Keep agents in separate working directories
Deny write permissions to LlamaFactory
Run gpt-researcher in a disposable workspace
Avoid shared git repositories
requires-engineering: add file-locking if shared state is later introduced

D_cascading_error.rationale: gpt-researcher produces research reports and citations that a downstream customer-support agent could treat as authoritative if an external workflow wires them together. LlamaFactory has no built-in verification or action controls in the profile, so the main risk is unverified A output becoming B input.
conditions: IF gpt-researcher outputs are copied into LlamaFactory prompts or tickets
IF the downstream workflow does not add human verification
mitigations: Require source checks before reuse
Insert a human approval step
Mark research outputs as untrusted by default
Limit downstream use to summaries only
requires-engineering: add automated citation validation

E_compliance.rationale: No explicit residency, retention, or regulated-data handling mismatch is documented for either agent, and both profiles are open-source docs-only. The only concrete compliance concern is that gpt-researcher can process local documents and send them to external APIs, while LlamaFactory has no comparable data flow, so the pair’s compliance exposure is limited and one-sided.
conditions: IF regulated data is placed into gpt-researcher inputs
IF external API providers are used without a DPA or residency review
mitigations: Exclude regulated data from research jobs
Use approved vendors only
Document retention settings for API providers
Purge temporary artifacts after each run
requires-engineering: implement data-class routing by policy
